name: Prefect (server: dashboard, runs, scheduler, workers, events)
param_style: SQLAlchemy 2.0 Core on aiosqlite: named :name binds, IN lists expanded per call; the worker poll is a Jinja-rendered text() query
schema_source: the pinned server's own SQLite Alembic migrations (prefect server database reset, head 27d8f4e1a6c9), dumped from sqlite_master; alembic_version left out
data_scale: scale 1: 60 flows, 120 deployments/schedules, 6 work pools, 18 queues, 30 workers; 12k past flow runs over 30 days, recency-skewed (3.9k in the last 24 h, 7.4k in 7 days; 46 % from 10 hot deployments), 380 scheduled; 36k flow run states; 36k task runs (one run fans out to 600) with 36k states; 16k logs; 1.2k artifacts; 7.2k events with 27.6k event_resources. ~151 MB, builds in ~1.5 s. Prefect rows are wide (UUID text keys, ~15 indexes per run table), so this is ~1/400 of the 5M-run tables in the issues
visibility_note: 24k stars; a widely used Python workflow orchestrator whose self-hosted server (prefect server start) defaults to SQLite
interest_note: Dashboard aggregates compiled from real SQLAlchemy builders: julianday/strftime time-bucketed run history, interval arithmetic in correlated CASE subqueries, EXISTS-over-json_each tag filters, the graph-v2 json_each x json_each edge CTE with json_group_array, a ROW_NUMBER worker-poll template, and strftime('%s') event histograms with first_value() windows.
reach_note: widely self-hosted by data teams; SQLite is the server's default database

cpu_evidence.summary: /flow_runs/history 24 h / 5-minute view times out: 289 buckets x ~96k in-window runs of a 5.2M-row flow_run (Postgres; the SQLite branch buckets with julianday instead)
dashboard /flow_runs/filter (24 h window, START_TIME_DESC, limit 41) reads and top-N sorts all 50.7k window rows: 375 ms on a 5.67M-row flow_run
/api/task_runs/count takes 10+ s on a SQLite server (3.5.0); fixed by PR #19548 replacing EXISTS subqueries with JOINs
API and UI super slow after upgrading to 3.x; PR #20940 added ix_task_run__state_type_start_time because the dashboard's four task-run counts were slow on 6M+ task runs
graph-v2 polled every second rebuilds the full graph: its WITH edges query was 68 % of DB time over 48 h for ~900-node runs, pinning a 1-vCPU database
a work pool with hundreds of flow runs per day: its page loads its flow runs ever slower until it cannot load them at all
SQLite server with ~1500 runs and a 1.1 GB database: Runs/Flows and Deployments pages take up to 35 s, with 'database is locked'
scheduler loop times out and stops scheduling once flow_run_state/task_run_state grow past 40 GB
server loop services overrun their intervals (RecentDeploymentsScheduler 7.5 s vs 5 s, FlowRunNotifications 6.8 s vs 4 s) with DB time-outs
